text: A queue only helps if workers eventually process faster than new work arrives. Little's law relates in-flight work to arrival rate times latency. At four hundred sixty requests a second and two tenths of a second, roughly ninety two requests are in flight on average. If latency quadruples, so does that count. Bound queues, cap per-client buffers, and use exponential backoff with jitter. Drop stale typing signals before you compromise accepted messages.
